_about: Learned parameters for the Indian Cove nowcast. Produced by the microclimate study (Phase 1/2), consumed by nowcast.py -> nowcast.json -> the board. Bias offsets fill in as join_log.csv accumulates real rain events; everything else is seeded from the Phase 1 measurements.
generated_note: seed built 2026-08-24 from phase1 beam/blockage run

radar.why: Both NEXRADs overshoot ~a mile over the cove (KATX 5661 ft @103 km, KLGX 4646 ft @92 km; measured blockage 0% / 14%). Low-level rain is invisible. Direct radar/MRMS reflectivity is near-useless here and must be down-weighted; model + surface obs carry the nowcast.

stations.precip_gauges_note: Synoptic rain gauges near the cove, closest first. G2160=Fair Harbor Marina Grapeview (2.8 mi, on the water; measured 2026-09-04, was previously noted as ~5 mi). G2480=GW2480 Grapeview is CLOSER at 2.4 mi and is now used for rain even when its faulty thermometer fails the temperature consensus -- see STATIONS.md. F9464=FW9464 CWOP station, south end of Harstine Island (~7.6 mi S, inland/elevated 252 ft) -- an on-island gauge, supplementary (citizen station, unverified gauge; scored by score.py). Tipping/citizen buckets under-catch light drizzle. Requires SYNOPTIC_TOKEN; falls back to keyless METAR when absent.

bias_offsets._status: awaiting rain events in join_log.csv; null = use raw value

stations.upwind_note: Per regime (wind_regimes[].upwind): stations UPWIND of the cove for that flow -- leading indicators for rain inbound. Bearings from cove: KSHN WSW, KOLM S, KTIW E, KTCM ESE, KPWT NNE. NW flow is data-sparse (Olympics/Hood Canal), so post-frontal-NW upwind is weak.
stations.wu_stations_note: TEN Weather Underground PWS within 4.7 km, closest-first. Found 2026-09-13 via api.weather.com/v3/location/near?product=pws -- we had only ever registered the two Tomas named, and never looked. All ten were live with rain gauges and qcStatus=1 when surveyed; eight also report solarRadiation. KWASHELT285 (0.56 km, Ecowitt GW3000) is Tomas's and the primary; KWASHELT12 (1.13 km, meteohub) has hourly history back to at least 2018 and is the backfill truth source. Most of the other eight reach back to 2023-2024. This takes SUB-DAILY rain gauges from 3 to 10, which clears the >=5-neighbour threshold the PWS rainfall QC scheme needs (see RESEARCH_NOTES.md). wu.py caches on disk because mini_cycle runs nowcast/score/cove_obs as separate processes and ten stations uncached is ~3,900 calls/day against a free key.

wu_station_notes.KWAGRAPE21: NO TEMPERATURE. Reports rain, solar and wind but tempAvg is null in both live and historical observations. Usable as a rain/solar peer for neighbour-relative QC; must NOT be counted as a temperature neighbour.
wu_station_notes.KWASHELT12: No solar sensor (meteohub). Deepest history of the set -- hourly back to at least 2018 -- and therefore the backfill truth source FOR TEMPERATURE ONLY. Its WIND is not trustworthy: over 168 matched hours it read exactly zero gust 37% of the time while KWASHELT285 never did, and its maximum gust in FIVE YEARS is 25.2 kt at a site that gets Small Craft Advisories. Sheltered, or the anemometer stalls below its starting threshold. Do not use it to evaluate wind forecasts or the board's wind wording.
wu_station_notes.KWASHELT285: Tomas's, Ecowitt GW3000, mounted ~20 ft up on the roof fascia in clean air -- the best-exposed PWS we have. Closest at 0.56 km, measures solar + UV. Over 168 matched hours it read 1.33x the gusts of KWASHELT12 and never once reported zero, which is what a properly exposed anemometer looks like. PRIMARY for wind. Brand new: NO history, accumulates forward only, so it cannot support any retrospective wind study yet.
wu_station_notes.KWALAKEB37: History only from 2026-07; shallowest of the set.

KWAGRAPE6.evidence: Identical temp/dewpt/RH/wind/solar from 2026-05 onward (100%, 98-100%, 94-100%, 93-100%, 88-100% of shared hours) against a 2024-2026-04 baseline of 29-71%, 2-56%, 0-90%, 16-69%, 20-71%. Confirmed against the WU API directly, not an ingest artefact.
KWAGRAPE6.why_it_hid: PRESSURE is 0% identical in every month, because each Ambient console derives sea-level pressure from its own configured elevation (82 ft vs 68 ft). It is the one field that stays independent when a sensor array is shared, and it is the field an earlier check used to clear the pair.
KWAGRAPE6.cause: Two separate registrations 350 m apart with different consoles and firmware (AMBWeatherV4.1.7 vs AMBWeatherV4.3.6), but one 915 MHz outdoor sensor array reaching both.
KWAGRAPE6.action: EXCLUDED from live medians and station counts. Still HARVESTED: its pre-2026-05 history is genuinely independent and worth keeping.

stations.wu_duplicates_note: Stations excluded from live medians because they are not independent observations. wu.independent_stations() applies this; harvest.py deliberately ignores it.

wind_regimes.name: frontal-SW
wind_regimes.note: onshore SW flow -- systems arrive from here

wind_regimes.name: pre-frontal-S
wind_regimes.note: veering ahead of a front, rain increasing

wind_regimes.name: post-frontal-NW
wind_regimes.note: showery, but convergence usually parks north of us

baro.note: surface pressure tendency (Open-Meteo pressure_msl or Tacoma PORTS). Falling fast => system inbound; boosts wet confidence.

blend._about: Crossfade from obs-extrapolation to model as lead time grows. weights sum ~1 across {minutely, hourly, regime}.

wind_shelter._about: Local wind = free-stream (forecast) speed x factor, per regime, per point; direction rotates by dir_shift deg. Factor = local speed / open-water free-stream. Look up by the wind_regimes[].name that the forecast direction falls in.
wind_shelter._method: WindNinja 3.12.2 on a fine custom landscape (windninja/cove_landscape.lcp, 5 m, built from 1 m LIDAR DTM+canopy). STRONG winds: momentum/CFD solver (OpenFOAM RANS) -- resolves the cliff-lee eddy that mass-conservation misses. LIGHT calm nights: mass-conserving + diurnal slope-flow + non-neutral stability -- cold-air drainage/pooling. Supersedes the earlier 30 m LANDFIRE mass-solver seed.

stable_night._about: Clear calm winter pre-dawn (05:00, 0 cloud, 3 kt ambient offshore). stable_kt = near-surface wind; the marina is nearly calm (~2 kt) and the drainage deepens it below the neutral baseline while exposed shores hold ~3.5 kt. stable_dir = direction the flow comes from (deg).

wind_shelter.notes: post-frontal-NW HarstinePointe_SW factor 1.54 is a terrain-gap/edge speedup with high CFD uncertainty -- treat as 'exposed/accelerated', not a precise value.
wind_shelter._speed_independent: Validated speed-independent: CFD at 15 vs 30 kt changed the marina factor by <=0.02 (mean |d|=0.004, max any point 0.05). So a single factor per regime applies at all strong-wind speeds; no speed axis needed. local = regional_kt x factor.
wind_shelter.solver: momentum: OpenFOAM RANS 300 it, 15 m mesh, neutral; drainage: mass-conserving diurnal + non_neutral_stability, 15 m mesh

model_calibration.note: add temp_offset_f to model temp; multiply model precip by precip_ratio (rain shadow)
model_calibration.precip_ratio_source: Jarrell Cove CoCoRaHS (US1WAMS0032) vs Open-Meteo, 862 days -- accurate hand-gauge, supersedes G2160

drainage_temp_adjust_f._note: Additional temperature correction by wind regime, CENTERED so it leaves the hour-of-day mean unchanged. Derived from 5.7 years of archived Open-Meteo forecasts against the network median: drainage nights run +1.55 F warmer in error than mechanical ones BEYOND the hour-of-day bias, same sign in 15 of 15 night hours, n=56-759 per cell. Apply the 'drainage' value when nowcast reports wind.mode == drainage, the 'mechanical' value otherwise.

surge_model.source: calibrate_surge.py: Tacoma residual vs Open-Meteo ERA5 pressure/wind
surge_model._note: surge_ft = a*(p0-pressure_hpa) + bu*ws_kt*sin(dir) + bv*ws_kt*cos(dir) + offset; anchored to live Tacoma residual, fading over anchor_hours.
